summary: Label the makrimo-wa box Infectum-wa
rationale: The only example in this box has makrimo-wa, and the supplied corpus confirms makrəmowa. It is the wa form of the Infectum and therefore belongs under Infectum-wa. The present box label omits -wa.

summary: Move 29/25 makrimo-wa from III Infectum to Infectum-wa.
rationale: The source and inherited token both contain -wa and describe past habitual hosting.

summary: Place 30/2 mkarmo 'hochgeehrt' under new II.2.
rationale: Being honoured corresponds to honouring a person, not the inherited intransitive gloss edelmütig werden. Preserve the existing form-box placement.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 1.1/62)

data.turoyo: I naqqa l nošo d uṯewole musafər, manṭanwo l qume ʕaqude w ḥarire apšoṯo w pastiq, sidayna u ḏ̣ayfo duwewo ʕazizo, hani mitakramwole.
data.translation: Wenn jemand Besuch bekam, servierte man ihm Süßwürste, Stücke von ḥărire, Rosinen und pāstīq. Ein geschätzter Gast wurde bei uns damit bewirtet.

rationale: New proposed III Detransitive Infectum-wa box; provisions and l-suffixed guest make impersonal hospitality construction explicit.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.21/3869)

data.turoyo: Bat 83 azzano, mətyaqnət qayimi nafiqi l qamuṯayna w makrəmallan ġalabe. Maḥətte u məklo, mamṭalle, azzan əmmi: "Kubʕena d əzzoxu mṣaletu ʕal u qawro du šex".
data.translation: We went after eighty-three. Certainly they get up, come out to meet us, and honour us greatly. He put down the food; they brought it. We went, and they said, “We want you to go and pray over the sheikh's grave.”

rationale: New III Preterit box, plural hosts and first-person plural guests, food context. English is verbatim project machine translation; semantic analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: New sense 2: (trans.) ehren, als Gast bewirten
rationale: 113/122 has hosts honouring an understood guest and serving coffee/tea. This differs from inherited edelmütig werden and explains existing Part. Pass. mkarmo 'hochgeehrt'. One new finite attestation plus the inherited state example.

summary: New sense 1: als Gast bewirtet werden (Detrans.; auch unpersönlich mit l-)

data.gloss: als Gast bewirtet werden (Detrans.; auch unpersönlich mit l-)

rationale: JTM 1.1/62 has hospitality provisions and mitakramwole with a guest suffix. Proposed Detransitive hospitality counterpart of III.1; one occurrence, morphological comparison with tkrm remains an editorial question.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (113/122)

data.turoyo: Komər qayimi me qume: "Ahla w sahla!" W yatu, mkaramme ġalabe w mqadammalle qaḥwa w čaye, štele, fayəš tloṯo yawme.
data.translation: Sie standen vor ihm auf: Willkommen! - Er setzte sich. Sie erwiesen ihm alle Ehre und setzten ihm Kaffee und Tee vor; er trank ihn und blieb dort

rationale: New II.2 honouring sense; hosts and guest in a complete hospitality sequence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.16/3562)

data.turoyo: Bdele kmakrəm u Mafəryono w hulele hadiyat stene. Mbasamle lebe ʕal d myaqarle, d ubele hadiye mede.
data.translation: He began honouring the maphrian and gave him gifts too. He gladdened his heart by honouring him, by giving him some gift.

rationale: First secure III Infectum after round 1 moved the old -wa quotation; explicit human honouree and gifts. English is verbatim project machine translation; semantic analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: ehren; (als Gastgeber) Gastmähler und Bewirtung darbieten
rationale: Clarifies the inherited doubtful darbieten: in 29/25 the direct objects are feasts, slaughterings and everything for guests. The Imperativ at 29/338 independently retains honouring a guest.

summary: II has a generosity reading at 30/27 and an external honouring/hosting reading at 113/122. The l-marked lu mṣaydono in 30/27 is compatible with an actor; the ambiguous place does not justify deleting its inherited meaning.

III honouring takes a guest in the Imperativ, but 29/25 names hospitality provisions as objects. The gloss clarifies that construction rather than interpreting every honouring event as physical offering.

Allowed lookup of tkrm shows mətkaramle/mətkarəm 'ehren' at 105/4, active and with an understood guest. This supports overlap but does not prove mitakramwole is that separate root. The III Detransitive analysis stays explicitly provisional.
No separately lexicalised light-verb idiom or new etymology is needed. Hospitality is supported by actual provisions, guest participants and serving actions, not free translation alone.
Jan English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. Senses rest on Turoyo alone; quoted English retains the supplied wording. This JSON contains only round-2 proposals.
Round 1 already corrected the old III Infectum example to Infectum-wa and linked II mkarmo to sense 2. Those corrections are retained, not proposed twice.
Arabic Ənta Abuna təkram and Abuna təkram are code-switched courtesy quotations. The reader’s IV is an Arabic label, not a new Turoyo stem or Detransitive Infectum box.

makrəmo has clear honoured-state semantics, but its vocalism alone does not secure III versus II mkarmo. It cannot widen the provisional round-1 III Detransitive hospitality sense without resolving morphology.
No new idiom or light-verb construction is established; honouring plus gifts/food remains within the existing and round-1 senses.
Confirm mitakramwole in JTM 1.1/62 as III Detransitive rather than tkrm I, and establish whether guest -le is a retained recipient in an impersonal construction.
Revisit the inherited ambiguous 30/27: is the hunter actor or beneficiary, and does mkaramle describe generosity or honouring? Retain II.1 until this is settled.
Are II and III honouring interchangeable, dialect-specific, or constructionally distinct? The small sample does not decide.
At Jan 2.1/12, is makrəmo a form of III or a vocalic variant of II mkarmo? Confirm before adding a new Part. Pass. box or widening the III Detransitive gloss.
In Arabic təkram at Jan 2.10/2295–2297, is the courtesy formula morphologically active or a conventional passive-like formula? This does not determine a Turoyo paradigm.
Jan independently supports round-1 honouring/hosting: the maphrian is honoured with gifts, and visitors with food. No new meaning is required.
makrəmo describes an honoured person and supports the honouring meaning recognised in round 1, but II versus III attribution remains unresolved; no Part. Pass. box is created from it.
